name: Build Your Own Strategy
tagline: Name and reuse a safe multi-step cornering behaviour.
narrative: The Snake Corridor repeatedly presents the same operation: turn into an open side and immediately advance. Conditions still belong in rules, where they are evaluated every tick. A function does something different: it names a fixed sequence of actions. Compose a turn-and-step function, then let an ordered rule decide when that sequence is appropriate.
objective: Solve the 11×11 Snake Corridor and use at least one custom multi-step function.
learningObjective: Separate decision logic from reusable behaviour: rules evaluate conditions, while functions execute fixed action sequences one action per tick.
intelligenceExplanation: The brain starts with four primitive bricks and no rules. The Functions tab is unlocked, so you can compose a fixed sequence such as pivot-left followed by step. A rule can call that function when the left side is open; other rules still handle straight movement, blocked routes, and arrival. A running function is checked for action safety before each primitive.
hint: Compose a `turn-left-and-step` function from [pivot-left, step], then call it only when the left side is open.
hints: Functions sequence actions; they do not contain WHEN checks. Keep sensing and branching in the rule list.
Create a two-step function: pivot-left, then step.
Use this order: atGoal → hold; !wallLeft → your turn-and-step function; !wallAhead → step; always → pivot-right.
brief: Build a reusable cornering function and use ordered rules to solve the Snake Corridor.
context: Rules decide when to act; a custom function packages a fixed action sequence.
